name: AML Screening Process
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for Anti-Money Laundering screening at FirstUK Bank, governed by the Financial Crime department and applicable to Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, and Branch Staff.

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The owner of the AML Screening SOP responsible for the oversight and maintenance of the procedure.

name: Financial Crime Staff
description: Staff members within the Financial Crime department designated as the target audience and executors of the AML screening procedure.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: Compliance Staff
description: Personnel responsible for ensuring the AML screening process adheres to regulatory and internal policy requirements.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: Branch Staff
description: Front-line personnel involved in the AML screening workflow as part of the designated audience for the SOP.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Staff, Compliance, Branch Staff

name: AML Screening Process
description: A systematic procedure designed to detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations by screening customers against regulatory lists.
context: Establish procedures for AML screening to detect and prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations through systematic screening of customers against regulatory lists.

name: New Customer Account Opening Process
description: A mandatory operational procedure governing the opening of all new customer accounts to ensure compliance and regulatory standards.
context: Applies to: All new customer account openings (mandatory)

name: Periodic Re-screening Process
description: A recurring review process for customers based on risk profile, with high-risk customers reviewed quarterly and standard customers reviewed annually.
context: Periodic re-screening (high-risk customers quarterly, standard annually)

name: Transaction Monitoring Process
description: An ongoing and automated workflow used to monitor financial transactions for irregularities or suspicious patterns.

name: Suspicious Activity Assessment and Reporting Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for assessing potentially suspicious activities and filing the necessary reports.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer classification that requires more frequent periodic re-screening on a quarterly basis.

name: Standard Customer
description: A customer classification subject to standard annual periodic re-screening.

name: Automated Monitoring System
description: The system responsible for the ongoing, automated execution of transaction monitoring.

name: AML Screening Process
description: An operational workflow to screen customer applications against lists to identify potential matches. The process is largely automated taking less than 5 minutes, but can extend to 1-24 hours if a manual review is required due to a hit.
context: Timeline: <5 minutes (automated), 1–24 hours (manual review if hit)

name: Initiate Screening
description: The first stage of the AML process where the screening procedure is triggered following the receipt of a customer application.

name: Screen Against Lists
description: The execution phase where the customer's data is checked against predefined lists to identify potential matches.

name: Assess Match
description: The analysis phase where a potential match identified during screening is evaluated to determine if it is a true hit.

name: Match Found Decision Gate
description: A branching point based on the result of the match assessment. If no match is found, the process proceeds; if a match is found, it triggers a manual review.

name: Record Results
description: The step where the outcomes of the screening and match assessment are formally documented in the system.

name: Hit Handling
description: An optional step performed only if a match was identified, involving the specific procedures to manage and resolve the hit.

name: AML Screening Completion Checkpoint
description: The final regulatory gate verifying that the AML screening process has been fully executed and recorded before the application can progress.

name: Automated Screening System
description: The system responsible for the automated portions of the screening process, completing these steps in under 5 minutes.

name: Manual Reviewer
description: The human actor responsible for conducting manual reviews when a match is found, with a processing window of 1 to 24 hours.

name: Applicant
description: The individual whose application has been received and is the subject of the AML screening process.

name: Customer Screening Process
description: An operational workflow triggered by new account openings, periodic schedules, or manual requests to screen customers against configured lists using legal identifiers.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Screening Initiation Step
description: The initial phase of the screening process where a trigger is identified and required customer information is gathered for system entry.

name: Screening System Data Entry
description: The action of entering customer identifiers into the screening system to prepare a query and execute the search against configured lists.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Compliance Staff
description: The human actor responsible for entering customer information into the screening system to initiate the query process.

name: Screening System
description: The automated system that prepares the screening query and executes the check against all configured lists based on the input data.
context: Initiates screening against all configured lists

name: Customer
description: The individual or business entity being screened, specifically during new account opening, periodic reviews, or manual requests.

name: New Customer Account
description: A customer account in the process of being opened, which serves as a trigger for the automatic screening process before creation is finalized.
context: New customer account opening (before account creation)

name: Screen Against Regulatory Lists
description: A mandatory screening step where the entity is checked against six specific regulatory and risk lists to identify sanctions, PEP status, or adverse media. Each list has specific update frequencies and distinct outcomes based on the type of hit discovered.

name: OFAC Sanctions Screening
description: A mandatory check against the US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list. It covers global individuals and entities under US sanctions and is updated daily.
context: Authority: US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control
List: Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN)

name: EU Consolidated Sanctions Screening
description: A mandatory check against the European Commission's EU Common Foreign & Security Policy sanctions list. It covers individuals and entities under EU sanctions and is updated daily.
context: List: EU Common Foreign & Security Policy sanctions

name: HM Treasury Sanctions Screening
description: A mandatory check against the UK Treasury (OFSI) sanctions designations list. It covers individuals and entities under UK sanctions and is updated daily.
context: Authority: UK Treasury (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation, OFSI)

name: UN Sanctions Screening
description: A mandatory check against the UN Security Council's Consolidated UN sanctions list regarding terrorism and weapons. This list is updated weekly.
context: List: Consolidated UN sanctions (terrorism, weapons, etc.)

name: PEP Database Screening
description: A real-time check against third-party providers (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones) to identify Politically Exposed Persons, including government officials and their associates.
context: Authority: Third-party data provider (World-Check, Dow Jones, etc.)
List: Politically Exposed Persons (government officials, senior politicians, military)

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: A daily check using news database aggregators to identify criminal convictions, fraud allegations, or sanctions violations related to the subject.
context: List: Criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations (from news)

name: Sanctions Hit Escalation Gate
description: A decision point triggered by any match on the OFAC, EU, HM Treasury, or UN sanctions lists, resulting in an immediate escalation.

name: PEP Match Review Gate
description: A decision point triggered by a PEP match which requires the process to move to enhanced due diligence rather than an automatic block.
context: Hits: PEP match = enhanced due diligence (not auto-block)

name: Adverse Media Assessment Gate
description: A decision point where material adverse media hits trigger an escalation for further assessment.
context: Hits: Material adverse media = escalation for assessment

name: Screening Execution Process
description: An automated operational workflow used to screen customers against configured lists to identify potential matches. The process is characterized by high-speed execution, typically returning results in under one minute.

name: Screening Engine
description: The automated system responsible for receiving customer names, searching configured lists, and identifying exact or close-match results based on a match threshold.
context: System enters customer name into screening engine
Screening engine searches all configured lists
System checks for exact and close-match results

name: Customer Name Submission
description: The initial step where the system inputs the customer's name into the screening engine to initiate the search.
context: System enters customer name into screening engine

name: List Search Execution
description: The phase where the screening engine scans all pre-configured lists to find potential matches for the submitted name.
context: Screening engine searches all configured lists

name: Match Validation Check
description: The step where the system evaluates results for both exact matches and close matches, considering name variations and typos.
context: System checks for exact and close-match results

name: Screening Results Retrieval
description: The final step of the automated process where results, including the matched name, list, and match score, are returned, usually within one minute.
context: Result includes: Matched name, list, match score

name: Match Threshold Determination
description: A configurable decision gate (typically set at 80%+) that determines if a result qualifies as a match based on name, DOB, and nationality.

name: Customer
description: The individual whose identity details (Name, DOB, Nationality) are being processed through the screening engine.
context: System enters customer name into screening engine

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for establishing a new customer account, involving KYC completion, screening results assessment, and AML compliance checks.
context: Proceed with account opening (KYC already complete)

name: Assess Screening Results
description: The stage where the outcome of sanctions and watchlist screening is reviewed to determine if the customer can proceed with account opening. In a no-match scenario, the action is immediate.

name: Record Screening Outcome
description: The action of documenting the 'screening passed' status in the system, including the specific screening date and the system reference number.
context: Note screening date and system reference

name: AML Compliance Checklist Review
description: The final step following a successful screening result where the operator continues to the AML compliance checklist.

name: Screening Result Validation
description: A decision gate checking for hits across sanctions lists, watchlists, and adverse media. A 'No Match' result allows the process to proceed to account opening.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists

name: Sanctions and Adverse Media Screening Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance gate that verifies the customer is not on any sanctions or watchlists and has no adverse media before proceeding with account opening.
context: Screening shows NO hits across all lists

name: Applicant
description: The individual undergoing the screening process to open an account.

name: Match Found Scenario Handling Process
description: The operational workflow triggered when an AML screening returns a potential hit during the account opening process. It involves stopping the onboarding, documenting the match, and escalating to the Financial Crime team.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: Screening Result Identification
description: The initial stage where the screening system identifies a potential hit, including the match score, matched name, and the specific list identified.

name: Account Opening Suspension
description: An immediate mandatory action to halt the account opening process once a potential AML match is detected.

name: Financial Crime Escalation
description: The action of transferring the case to the Financial Crime team for a specialized manual review of the potential match.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: Match Detail Documentation
description: The requirement to record the specific details of the identified match within the bank's system for audit and review purposes.

name: Manual Review Initiation
description: The final step in the immediate action sequence to start the formal manual review process of the flagged entity.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: The specialized team responsible for performing manual reviews of potential AML screening hits to determine if a true match exists.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime team for manual review

name: AML Screening Match Gate
description: A branching point where the presence of a potential hit (match found) triggers the suspension of account opening and escalation to the Financial Crime team.

name: AML Screening Compliance Checkpoint
description: The mandatory regulatory gate that verifies whether the applicant appears on sanctions or AML lists before allowing an account to be opened.

name: Manual Review Process (Hit Assessment)
description: An operational workflow used to assess potential matches generated during screening. It involves a preliminary assessment of match scores and personal details to determine if a hit is a false positive or a true positive.

name: Preliminary Assessment Step
description: The initial stage of the Manual Review Process where Financial Crime Staff evaluate a match based on score, name variance, date of birth, nationality, and entity type.
context: Financial Crime Staff Reviews: 1. Match Score... 2. Name Variance... 3. Date of Birth... 4. Nationality... 5. Business

name: Financial Crime Staff
description: The personnel responsible for conducting the preliminary assessment of screening hits and determining the initial decision outcome.

name: Hit Outcome Decision
description: A branching point based on the preliminary assessment that determines if a hit is a clear false positive, a likely true positive requiring immediate escalation, or an uncertain match requiring deeper research.
context: A) Clear False Positive: Similar name but different person → Clear to proceed
B) Likely True Positive: Name, DOB, nationality all match → Escalate immediately
C) Uncertain: Partial match requiring investigation → Deeper research

name: True Positive Investigation Process
description: The operational workflow for investigating and actioning confirmed true positive matches resulting from AML screening, including categorization by hit type and required remediation.

name: Identify Match Reason
description: The action of determining the specific list and designation that triggered the match, such as sanctions, PEP, or adverse media.
context: Identify Reason: Which list? What's the designation (sanctions, PEP, adverse media)?

name: Determine Remediation Action
description: The stage where the specific action is decided based on the type of hit, ranging from account freezes to enhanced due diligence or risk monitoring.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI
PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required

name: Document Investigation Findings
description: The formal recording of the investigation, capturing match assessment notes, decision reasoning, evidence reviewed, and the approver's details.

name: Hit Type Categorization Gate
description: A branching point that determines the workflow path based on whether the hit is a Sanctions Hit, PEP Hit, or Adverse Media hit.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI
PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required (escalate to Compliance Head)
Adverse Media: Risk assessment (may proceed with monitoring)

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior authority responsible for reviewing and approving actions related to PEP hits and enhanced due diligence.

name: OFSI (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation)
description: The external regulatory body to which sanctions hits must be escalated following an account freeze.

name: External Regulatory Escalation — OFSI
description: The highest level of escalation triggered by a confirmed sanctions hit, requiring a mandatory account freeze and reporting to the regulator.
context: Sanctions Hit: Automatic FREEZE + Escalate to OFSI

name: Sanctions Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory control point where a confirmed sanctions hit triggers an automatic freeze of assets.

name: PEP Compliance Gate
description: A control point that identifies Politically Exposed Persons and mandates the application of enhanced due diligence.
context: PEP Hit: Enhanced due diligence required

name: Frozen Account
description: An account that has been automatically frozen as a result of a confirmed sanctions hit.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for opening a customer account, which includes a specific sub-workflow for resolving false positive screening matches.

name: False Positive Resolution Step
description: A discrete stage in the account opening process where a potential match is determined to be a false positive. The step requires documenting reasoning, recording the result in the system to prevent re-flagging, and archiving the assessment within a 2–4 hour timeline.

name: False Positive Determination Gate
description: A branching condition to determine if a screening alert is a false positive. If determined as a false positive, the process proceeds to documentation and account opening.

name: Operational Reviewer
description: The actor responsible for determining false positives, documenting the reasoning for the distinction between persons, and recording the outcome in the system.

name: Screening Match Clearance Checkpoint
description: The mandatory compliance gate where a screening alert must be resolved as a false positive before the account opening process is permitted to proceed.

name: Record Screening Results
description: The final stage of the screening process where results, including reference numbers, match scores, and decisions, are documented in the system. This ensures a full audit trail of the screening outcome and the approver's resolution.
context: Record Fields: Screening reference number (system-generated), Customer ID, Screening date/time
If reviewed: Decision, approver, resolution date

name: System Approver
description: The individual responsible for reviewing screening hits and recording the final decision and resolution date within the system record.
context: If reviewed: Decision, approver, resolution date

name: Screening Outcome Decision
description: A decision gate based on the screening results that categorizes the customer as Pass or Hit, and subsequently assigns a status of Cleared, Blocked, or Under Review.

name: Account Management System (AMS)
description: The primary system used for storing screening records, linking results to customer records, and maintaining data for audit purposes.

name: AML Data Retention Check
description: A mandatory regulatory control requiring that all screening records be retained for a minimum of 5 years in accordance with AML regulations.

name: Screened Customer
description: The customer subject to the screening process whose ID is linked to the screening record in the AMS.

name: Sanctions Hit Handling Process
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for managing Sanctions Hits from OFAC, EU, HMT, and UN. It involves immediate account freezing, regulatory notification to OFSI within 24 hours, SAR filing, and a strict prohibition on tipping off the customer.
context: Timeline: Immediate + regulatory notification within 24 hours

name: Immediate Account Freeze
description: The initial action where the account is frozen immediately to ensure no transactions are permitted following a sanctions hit.

name: Compliance and Financial Crime Escalation
description: The action of escalating the sanctions hit to the Compliance Head and the Head of Financial Crime for review.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head + Head of Financial Crime

name: OFSI Regulatory Notification
description: The mandatory reporting of a UK sanctions hit to the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) within a 24-hour window.
context: Notify OFSI (UK Treasury) within 24 hours (if UK sanctions hit)

name: SAR Filing with NCA
description: The formal submission of a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) to the National Crime Agency (NCA) following a sanctions match.
context: File Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with NCA

name: System Documentation of Hold
description: The administrative step of recording the specific reason for the account hold within the bank's internal systems.

name: Anti-Tipping Off Communication Management
description: Ensuring the customer is not informed of the specific reason for the freeze to avoid tipping off risks; uses generic messaging.
context: Do NOT inform customer of reason (tipping off risk)
Generic message: "Your account has been frozen pending review"

name: Compliance Head
description: A senior officer responsible for receiving escalations regarding sanctions hits and overseeing the resolution.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head + Head of Financial Crime

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: A senior officer responsible for reviewing sanctions hits and coordinating with regulatory bodies.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head + Head of Financial Crime

name: OFSI (UK Treasury)
description: The external regulatory body that must be notified within 24 hours of a UK sanctions hit.
context: Notify OFSI (UK Treasury) within 24 hours (if UK sanctions hit)

name: NCA
description: The agency responsible for receiving Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs).
context: File Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with NCA

name: Manager
description: The actor to whom a case is escalated if a customer questions the generic freeze notification.
context: Escalate to manager if customer questions

name: Sanctions Hit Confirmation Gate
description: The decision point determining if a sanctions hit is a false positive or a true positive, leading to either unfreezing the account or maintaining the freeze/closing the account.
context: Hit confirmed as false positive → Unfreeze, apologize, proceed
Hit confirmed as true positive → Remain frozen, potential account closure

name: Sanctions Screening Checkpoint
description: The control gate where matches against OFAC, EU, HMT, and UN lists are processed and determined to be true or false positives.

name: Frozen Account
description: A customer account that has been placed under an immediate block, prohibiting all transactions due to a sanctions hit.
context: Your account has been frozen pending review

name: PEP Hit Handling Process
description: The procedure for managing customers identified as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs). It involves enhanced due diligence (EDD) rather than an automatic block, with a completion timeline of 1–2 business days.
context: Action: ENHANCED DUE DILIGENCE (Not automatic block)

name: PEP Status Flagging
description: The initial action of marking the customer record with a 'PEP' flag to initiate the enhanced workflow.

name: Compliance Head Escalation
description: The step where the PEP hit is escalated to the Compliance Head for formal review.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head for review

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior compliance officer responsible for reviewing PEP escalations and making the approval decision on whether to proceed with the application.
context: Escalate to Compliance Head for review

name: PEP Risk Assessment
description: The evaluation of the customer's specific PEP profile, determining if they are a family member, close associate, or a foreign PEP.
context: Assess risk (family member? Close associate? Foreign PEP?)

name: EDD Proceed or Reject Decision
description: A critical decision gate where the Compliance Head decides whether to proceed with Enhanced Due Diligence or reject the application entirely.
context: Approval decision: Proceed with EDD / Reject application

name: EDD Monitoring Implementation
description: The application of enhanced monitoring requirements if the decision to proceed with the application is made.

name: Risk Assessment Documentation
description: The final step of formalizing and recording the risk assessment results in the bank's records.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification Check
description: A mandatory compliance gate under EDD requirements to verify the beneficial ownership of the customer.

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: A mandatory requirement to collect and verify documentation regarding the customer's source of funds.

name: Quarterly Transaction Monitoring
description: An ongoing EDD requirement involving the review of transactions every quarter.

name: Annual PEP Review
description: A mandatory annual review of the PEP status and associated risk assessment.

name: PEP Customer
description: A customer flagged as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), including family members and close associates.
context: Assess risk (family member? Close associate? Foreign PEP?)

name: Adverse Media Hit Risk Assessment Process
description: A procedure for reviewing and assessing the materiality of adverse media hits during a banking relationship application. The process determines whether to proceed with monitoring or reject the application and is completed within 1–2 business days.

name: Review Adverse Media Details
description: The initial step where the actor reviews the specific news or adverse media details associated with the hit.

name: Assess Materiality
description: The evaluation of whether the adverse media information is relevant to the specific banking relationship.

name: Escalate to Compliance Head
description: A mandatory action taken when adverse media is deemed material, involving the notification and review by the Compliance Head.
context: If material: Escalate to Compliance Head

name: Application Proceed or Reject Decision
description: A branching point where a decision is made to either proceed with standard monitoring or reject the application based on the materiality and nature of the hit (e.g., old accusations vs recent sanctions violations).
context: Decision: Proceed with monitoring / Reject application
PASS: Old fraud accusation (10+ years ago, no conviction) → Proceed with standard monitoring
REJECT: Recent sanctions violation (confirmed) → Reject application

name: Document Assessment
description: The final step of the process where the findings and the outcome of the risk assessment are formally documented.

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior authority responsible for reviewing material adverse media hits and providing a decision on the application.

name: Adverse Media Materiality Check
description: A compliance gate used to determine if a news hit is material enough to trigger an escalation or an application rejection.
context: If material: Escalate to Compliance Head

name: Applicant
description: The individual or entity whose application is being evaluated for adverse media hits.

name: Ongoing Monitoring Process
description: A procedure for the continuous oversight of customers after initial screening, featuring differentiated monitoring frequencies and intensities based on the customer's risk profile (High-Risk vs Standard-Risk).

name: High-Risk Customer Quarterly Re-screening
description: A mandatory quarterly action for high-risk customers involving the re-scanning of sanctions lists to ensure continued compliance.
context: High-Risk Customers: Quarterly re-screening (re-scan sanctions lists)

name: High-Risk Enhanced Transaction Monitoring
description: The application of intensified monitoring on transactions for customers classified as high-risk.

name: Manual Review of Unusual Activity Alerts
description: A manual review process for alerts triggered by unusual activity specifically for high-risk customers.

name: High-Risk Annual Comprehensive Risk Review
description: A full-scale review of the customer's risk profile conducted on an annual basis for high-risk individuals.

name: Standard-Risk Customer Annual Re-screening
description: A yearly action for standard-risk customers involving the re-scanning of sanctions lists.
context: Standard-Risk Customers: Annual re-screening (re-scan sanctions lists)

name: Automated Transaction Monitoring
description: The use of automated systems to monitor transactions for standard-risk customers.

name: Automated Alert Review
description: The process where monitoring alerts for standard-risk customers are reviewed by automated rules rather than manual intervention.

name: Customer Risk Classification Gate
description: A branching point that determines whether a customer follows the High-Risk monitoring path (quarterly scans, manual review) or the Standard-Risk path (annual scans, automated review).

name: Transaction Monitoring Trigger Check
description: A set of conditional triggers (amount, jurisdiction, beneficiary, velocity) that, if met, initiate specific monitoring or investigation actions.
context: Rapid transaction velocity (multiple in short time)

name: Automated Monitoring System
description: The system responsible for executing automated transaction monitoring and applying automated rules to review alerts for standard-risk customers.

name: Sanctions List Re-screening Checkpoint
description: The mandatory regulatory gate where customers are re-screened against sanctions lists either quarterly or annually depending on risk level.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer subject to enhanced monitoring, quarterly re-screening, and annual comprehensive risk reviews.

name: Standard-Risk Customer
description: A customer subject to standard annual re-screening and automated transaction monitoring.

name: Monitored Transaction
description: Financial events subjected to monitoring, particularly those triggering alerts due to size, jurisdiction, or velocity.
context: Rapid transaction velocity (multiple in short time)

name: Screening System Down Troubleshooting Process
description: An operational procedure to handle scenarios where the screening system is unavailable during account opening. It mandates a halt to onboarding until the system is restored and screening is completed.

name: Outage Documentation Step
description: The initial action taken when the screening system is unavailable, requiring the staff to record the specific time the outage occurred.

name: Account Opening Suspension Step
description: A mandatory hold on the account opening process due to the criticality of screening.
context: Do NOT proceed with account opening (screening mandatory)

name: Technology Team Escalation Step
description: The action of notifying the Technology team to ensure immediate resolution of the system outage.

name: System Restoration Retry Step
description: The requirement to attempt the screening process again once the system has been restored.

name: Account Opening Delay Finalization
description: The final state where the account opening remains paused until all screening requirements are successfully met.
context: Account opening delayed until screening complete

name: Technology Team
description: The internal team responsible for the immediate resolution of screening system outages.

name: Screening System Availability Check
description: A check to determine if the screening system is functional; if unavailable, the process diverts to the troubleshooting workflow.

name: Mandatory Screening Compliance Gate
description: A critical regulatory gate that prevents the account opening process from proceeding if screening cannot be performed.
context: Do NOT proceed with account opening (screening mandatory)
Account opening delayed until screening complete

name: False Positive Screening Resolution Process
description: An operational workflow for managing customers who frequently trigger alerts during screening processes. It focuses on documenting previous assessments and updating profiles to accelerate future resolutions.
context: If Customer Frequently Hit on Screening

name: Document Previous False Positive Assessments
description: The initial action of recording and archiving the outcomes of prior screening assessments to justify subsequent false positive determinations.

name: Update Customer Profile with Verified Flag
description: Updating the customer's electronic record to include a 'verified' flag, intended to streamline the resolution of future screening hits.

name: Perform Rapid Re-screen Resolution
description: The action of resolving a re-screen trigger quickly, acknowledging that list updates may still cause a hit despite previous verification.
context: Re-screen may still trigger (due to list updates), but quick resolution

name: Implement Alternative Name Variant
description: Evaluating and applying an alternative name variant for the customer to reduce the frequency of screening hits and enable faster processing.
context: Consider alternative name variant for faster screening

name: Screening Analyst
description: The implicit actor responsible for documenting assessments, updating customer profile flags, and managing the re-screening resolution.

name: Frequently Triggered Customer
description: A customer who repeatedly triggers hits during AML or sanctions screening, necessitating a specific resolution workflow.
context: If Customer Frequently Hit on Screening

name: Screening Hit Verification Gate
description: The regulatory control point where a customer's name is screened against lists; this specific process manages the 'false positive' outcome of this gate.
context: Re-screen may still trigger (due to list updates)

name: Screening Audit Process
description: A quality assurance procedure consisting of monthly and annual audits to ensure screening decisions are properly escalated, documented, and timely. The process verifies hit resolution and the appropriateness of SAR filings.

name: Monthly Screening Decision Review
description: A monthly operational step where 10 or more screening decisions are reviewed to verify escalation accuracy, documentation of false positives, and decision timeliness.

name: Annual Full Screening Process Review
description: A comprehensive annual review of the screening process, including verification of active list coverage, hit resolution speed, and the appropriateness of SAR filings.

name: Screening Decision Compliance Gate
description: A control point within the audit process to ensure all screening lists are active and that hit resolutions and SAR filings meet regulatory appropriateness and timeliness standards.

name: AML Screening Process
description: An operational workflow focused on Anti-Money Laundering screening. It is positioned as Step 5 within the broader Account Opening process and follows the KYC verification procedure.

name: Account Opening Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for opening a new customer account, which includes AML screening as its fifth operational step.

name: KYC Verification Process
description: The Know Your Customer verification procedure that must be completed before AML screening can commence.

name: AML Screening Execution Step
description: The fifth specific action within the Account Opening process dedicated to performing AML screening.

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The individual responsible for the authorship and updating of the SOP, including the addition of hit handling procedures and ongoing monitoring.

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: A senior executive role responsible for the approval and sign-off of the operational procedure documents.
context: Approved by: Head of Financial Crime

name: Head of Compliance
description: A senior executive role responsible for the approval and sign-off of the operational procedure documents.
